origins: Many people have experienced a cold look, a gossip circle, or a sermon that felt like a finger pointing at them. Some of us were judged for divorce, doubt, addiction, appearance, or politics. After that, it feels safer to expect judgment from every believer than to risk it again.
teaches: Jesus said, “Do not judge, or you will be judged,” and warned believers about the measure they use. When the woman caught in adultery stood before Him, He asked, “Woman, where are your accusers? Has no one condemned you?” Then He said, “neither do I condemn you.” James writes, “Mercy triumphs over judgment.” Paul adds that “there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.” Some Christians fail to reflect Jesus, but He does not fail to reflect Himself. The Savior who welcomed sinners is the standard, not the critics.
self_statements: They will look down on me.
If they knew, they would condemn me.
I do not meet their standards.
It is safer to stay away.
errors: Treating all Christians as judges because of some.
Assuming I know what they think.
Feeling judged and concluding that I am.
questions: Who judged me, and what exactly did they do or say?
Have any Christians shown me grace?
How did Jesus treat people others judged?
Is judgment by some people a reason to avoid all people?
What would a gracious community look like?
Is there one safe person I could try again with?
truth: Jesus does not condemn me, and He calls His people to mercy, not judgment. Some Christians fall short of that, but I can look for those who reflect His grace. I do not have to let past judgment keep me from the fellowship God offers.
hw_truths: There is no condemnation in Christ.
Judgment by some does not define all.
I can find a safe community.
log: Each week, write one example of grace shown by a believer.
actions: Write what happened and how it made you feel.
Notice how Jesus treated the accused.
Find one believer who shows mercy and spend time with them.
Pray for the people who judged you.
prayer: Lord Jesus, You did not condemn the woman, and You do not condemn me. Heal the hurt from judgment and lead me to Your people who show mercy. Amen.
hw_questions: How did Jesus treat the judged?
What would a gracious church look like?
name_example: Sarah can write: “There is no condemnation for me in Christ Jesus.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “Christians will judge me.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
